prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universal “best” HVAC company for every situation in Phoenix — the right contractor depends on your location, the problem, your budget, and whether you need emergency service or a full replacement. I can help you find top local options if you tell me your ZIP code and what’s wrong with the system. Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical plan you can use now to find a good HVAC company and evaluate quotes.

What I need from you
- Your ZIP code (Phoenix is large).  
- A short description of the problem (no cooling, noisy, leaking, short-cycling, blowing warm air, etc.).  
- Whether you need same-day service or can wait for scheduled appointments.  

How to pick a good Phoenix HVAC contractor
- Verify license: Arizona contractors must be registered with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC). Ask for the ROC license number and confirm it on the ROC site.  
- Ask for proof of insurance (liability + workers’ comp).  
- Look for NATE-certified technicians and EPA 608 certification (required for refrigerant work).  
- Read recent Google, Yelp, and BBB reviews — prioritize recent, local feedback.  
- Get at least three written estimates with itemized parts/labor, permit requirements, and warranty terms.  
- Check warranties: parts vs. labor vs. system replacement, and how long they honor workmanship.  
- Ask if they install and service your system brand (some techs know certain brands better).

Red flags
- High-pressure sales or “today only” discounts pushing a full replacement without diagnostics.  
- No written estimate or vague scope of work.  
- Contractor refuses to show ROC number, proof of insurance, or references.  
- Very low bid that’s substantially below others (could be hidden fees or poor parts).

Questions to ask a contractor
- What’s the diagnostic fee and will it be applied to the repair?  
- Is your technician NATE-certified and EPA 608 certified?  
- Can you provide your ROC license number and insurance proof?  
- What’s included in the quoted price (parts, labor, permits)?  
- What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?  
- Do you offer financing or maintenance plans?

Typical Phoenix price ranges (rough, 2024)
- Thermostat replacement: $100–$350 (basic smart thermostat more).  
- Capacitor or contactor replacement: $100–$350.  
- Refrigerant recharge (small leak repair not included): $150–$450.  
- Evaporator coil replacement: $800–$2,000+.  
- Compressor replacement: $1,200–$3,500+.  
- Full system (AC + furnace/air handler) replacement: $4,000–$12,000+ depending on tonnage & efficiency.

Quick troubleshooting you can do now
- Check/reset the breaker for the A/C.  
- Replace a dirty air filter.  
- Ensure registers are open and outdoor unit is clear of debris.  
- If the outdoor fan isn’t turning, turn the system off and call a pro—do not try to run with the compressor locked.

If you want, give me your ZIP code and a short description of what’s happening and I’ll pull together a short list of well-reviewed local Phoenix HVAC companies and what to watch for with each.
